about: The second part of the epilogue, in which the king turns from the charge to later kings to the reward and the punishment: first a long blessing for the man who respects the stele, then the first curses on the man who does not. The blessing opens with a “whoever” in the style of the laws: if that man has good judgment and can guide his land aright, let him heed the words written on the stele, let the stele show him the way, the guidance, the verdicts and the rulings, let him guide the black-headed people, judge their cases, root out the wicked and the evil, and bring his people well-being (xli 75–94). Hammurabi names himself, king of justice, to whom Shamash gave truths; his words are weighty and his deeds have no rival (xli 95–102). A stretch follows that I cannot read (xli 103 – xlii 1). Then the blessing proper: if that man has heeded the words and has not effaced, overruled or changed the king’s verdict, words and designs, then he, a king of justice like Hammurabi, is wished a long scepter and a people shepherded in justice (xlii 2–17). The first curse begins at xlii 18: the man who ignores the words, forgets the curses, fears not the curse of the gods, blots out the king’s verdicts and designs, erases the inscribed name and writes his own, or has someone else do it — whether king, lord, governor or any person with a name — is cursed in turn by three deities: the great god, father of the gods, is asked to turn the glory of kingship away from him, to break his scepter and to curse his fates (xlii 39–52); Ellil, the lord who fixes the fates, is to decree for him a reign of sighing, few days, years of famine, darkness without light and sudden death, and to pronounce the ruin of his city, the scattering of his people and the loss of his name (xlii 53–80); and Bēlit, the great mother, is to turn his word to evil before Ellil, and to have the overthrow of his land and the pouring out of his life like water set on him (xlii 81–97). The numbers in the margin are the stele’s own line numbers, not law numbers. Several readings are uncertain, and the notes say where: the unread lines at xli 103–105, the verb uštepiel, the name of the god at xlii 45, the stretch xlii 59–63, the words šūbilam and igirrû, and the reading of the goddess’s name (Harper’s Bēlit, written NIN.LÍL). In xlii 5–9 Harper’s print has one divider too few; the plate and his own glossary show that a-wa-ti-ia (7), la uš-te-pi-el (8) and u-zu-ra-ti-ia (9) are three separate lines. The text below keeps his division, so a-wa-ti-ia la uš-te-pi-el stands on one written line (7), u-zu-ra-ti-ia on the next (8), then line 10.

sentences.i: If that man has discernment and is able to guide his land aright,
sentences.n: A new part of the epilogue begins, and it turns to blessing: a long “if”, whose good result the king then spells out. Read it like the laws’ šumma-clauses: šumma awīlum šū is “if that man” (šū after the noun is “that one, the man in question”), followed by the conditions. tašīmtam īšuma is tašīmtum “discernment, good judgment” (Harper’s tasimtu, “wisdom, diplomacy”) + īšu “he has” (išûm) + -ma “and”, which ties this clause to the next. mātassu is mātum “land” + -šu “his”: the t of the noun and the š of the suffix are said ss and written with the ZU sign (Harper’s ma-zu), the way šarrūssu is written in xlii 75. šutēšuram is the Št infinitive of ešērum “to be straight” (Harper’s “to rule with right”) in the accusative, “to guide aright”; ileʾʾi “he is able” (leʾûm; Harper’s i-li-i) comes last, as the verb does.

sentences.i: let him pay heed to the words that I wrote on my stele, and
sentences.n: The result of the blessing begins: “then let him …”. ana awâtim is “to the words” (awâtim, the plural of awātum in the genitive after ana); ša ina narûya ašṭuru is a relative clause, “which on my stele I wrote”, with its verb last and in the subjunctive (-u), as in xli 62. liqūlma is li- (“let him”) + qūl + -ma, the precative of qâlum “to heed”. Harper files li-gul-ma and the later i-gul-ma (xlii 5, 22) under QALU, “to give attention to”, so I normalize the verb as qâlum; the sign he reads gul is kept as he writes it in the reading line. The root and the vowels are not settled, and the sense is Harper’s: UNCERTAIN. The -ma joins this clause to the next two units.

sentences.i: the way, the guidance, the verdicts that I gave for the land, the rulings that I decided for the land,
sentences.n: Four things are listed one after another with no “and”; the verb that governs them is likallimšuma in the next unit (“let that stele show him …”). kibsam is kibsum “tread, way, procedure” (Harper’s kibsu, from kabāsum “to tread”); rīdam is “guidance, leadership”, as in xl 6. dīn mātim ša adīnu and purussê mātim ša aprusu are the two clauses of xli 68: “the verdict of the land that I judged, the decision of the land that I decided”. mâtim is written with the sign KALAM “land” (Harper’s circumflex marks a Sumerogram), read mātim. adīnu: Harper files a-di-nu under dânum “to judge, to decide” (his danu I,1, with i-di-in in §6 and li-di-in at xli 88); his glossary lists this very word, a-di-nu, at xli 69 (the parallel line in the part before), at xli 81 and at xlii 27, all under that verb. dīn adīnu is then “the verdict I judged”, a verb and its own noun, as dīnam idīn in §5. The part before (epilogue-1, xli 68) took the same word as addinu, nadānum “I gave”; one d cannot settle that, but Harper’s grouping and the paired noun and verb favour dânum, so it is read the same way in all three places here. Both readings make a verdict, so the English is the same, “the verdicts that I gave”.

sentences.n: The subject of the wish at last: narûm šū “that stele” (šū again “that one”). likallimšuma is li- + kallim, the precative of the D-stem of kalāmum “to show” (as at xli 12), + -šu “to him” + -ma “and”: “let it show him”. sentences.i: I am Hammurabi, the king of justice, to whom Shamash gave truths.
sentences.n: The king speaks of himself again, in a nominal sentence with anāku “I (am)” at the end, as at xl 10. Ḫammurabi šar mīšarim is “Hammurabi, king of justice” (the sign LUGAL read šar, “king of”, with mīšarim “of justice”, the title of xl 75 and xli 7). ša Šamaš kīnātim išrukušum is a relative clause with the verb in the subjunctive: “to whom Shamash gave truths”. išrukušum is išruk (the preterite of šarākum “to give”) + the subjunctive -u + -šum “to him”, the -u short before -šum, and the -šum looks back to Hammurabi: “the one to whom Shamash gave”. kīnātim is the plural of kittum “truth” (the litany’s lemma; kīnātum is the plural of kittum, from the root of kīnum “firm”; Harper lists ki-na-tim under his kinatu “justice”). The plate (Plate 76, row 97) shows the god’s star before UTU; Harper writes his name Šamaš.

sentences.i: Except [for la-ḫa ZI-IM.RI.GA, which I cannot read]; for the wise (?) …
sentences.n: This stretch I cannot read, and I read as little of it as the evidence allows. e-la carries a footnote in Harper’s print: “Peiser, e-la a-na la-ḫa-zi-im ri-qa”, that is, Peiser takes la-ḫa and the capital signs ZI-IM.RI.GA as la-ḫa-zi-im and ri-qa. e-la itself looks like ēla “except, apart from”, but that is a guess from the spelling. la-ḫa and ZI-IM.RI.GA Harper gives as bare signs (capitals, without a reading), which means he could not read them as words: I keep them unread. a-na is ana “to, for”. im-ki-im is entered in Harper’s glossary as IM-KI-IM (?), an unsettled word; as emqum is “wise” (the litany’s im-qum is said emqum), emqim “of the wise one (?)” would fit the signs (IM can be read em; KI read qi₂), but I keep Harper’s spelling and mark the reading uncertain. On the plate (Plate 76) line 103 is e-la a-na la-ḫa; lines 104 and 105 stand in one ruled box with two half-height rows (ZI-IM.RI.GA above, a-na im-ki-im below). Harper’s own numerals agree with taking them as two lines: his print puts the numeral 105 at a-na im-ki-im, straight after ZI-IM.RI.GA (so ZI-IM.RI.GA is 104), and the column ends there.

sentences.i: If that man — as to my words, which I wrote on my stele —
sentences.n: The first of the curses. It opens exactly like the second “if” at xlii 2–5, with the same words and the same relative clause (ša ina narûya ašṭuru, verb last), but this man is the one who disobeys. The sentence hangs in the air until the next unit, which gives the verbs: “… and has not heeded, and …”. The unit is a new paragraph because the curses begin here. On the plate the signs of xlii 19 (a-wa-ti-ia) are partly drawn in outline, that is, worn or broken on the stone; the reading is not in doubt, since the same words stand at xlii 3 and 29.

sentences.i: may the great god, the father of the gods, who named my reign, turn the glory of kingship away from him,
sentences.n: A god is called on to take the kingship from the man: ilum rabûm abu ilī nābû palêya, “the great god, father of the gods, who named my reign”. ilum is the AN sign alone (read DINGIR “god”), which Harper reads ilum and does not name; abu is abum “father” in the form before a genitive; ilī is again NI.NI, the plural “gods”; nābû is the participle of nabûm “to name” (Harper’s nabu I,1); palêya is palûm “reign” + -ia, the BAL sign (Harper’s sign list no. 7, palû). The god is not named in the line: the titles (“great god, father of the gods”) point to Anum, but that is my inference. melam šarrūtim “the glory of kingship”: ME.LAM is melammum, “the awe-inspiring radiance” of a god or king (Harper’s melammu “glory”). litēršu is Harper’s li-te-ir-šu, taru II,1 (D), li- + the D of târum + -šu “from him / to him”: the D means “to turn back, give back”, so “let him turn it away from him” is my reading of the wish (UNCERTAIN: “let him take back from him”).

sentences.n: Two more wishes of the same god. ḫaṭṭašu lišbir: GIŠ.PA-šu “his scepter” (as at xlii 14, where the obedient man was to have it lengthened) and lišbir, li- + išbir, šebērum “to break”. šīmātišu lirur: šīmātum, the plural of šīmtum “fate”, + -šu, and lirur is li- + irur, the precative of arārum “to curse” (Harper’s araru I,1, with li-ru-ur-šu at xliv 89). sentences.n: A second god is called, with his titles. Harper prints his name Bêl, “lord”, which is the sign group {d}EN.LÍL, as at xl 64 (the star, then EN and KID); I write Ellil, as in epilogue-1, and bēlum “the lord” follows in syllables. Harper’s own glossary has BEL [EN.LIL], god, whose chief seat of worship was Nippur, at xlii 53, 89 and 95, and his List of Signs (no. 49) shows the group star + EN + KID, so the identification is his, not mine. mušīm šīmātim “who fixes the fates” (mušīm, the D participle of šâmum “to decide, fix”, Harper’s samu II,1; šīmātim the plural of šīmtum). ša kibīssu lā uttakkaru “whose command is not altered”: kibītum “speech, command” + -šu, the ssu written with ZU (Harper’s ki-be-zu), and uttakkaru the passive of the D of nakārum with the -u of the relative clause (Harper’s nakaru II,2, ut-ta-ka-ru). mušarbû šarrūtīya “who makes my kingship great”: the Š participle of rabûm (Harper’s rabu III,1 “to enlarge, make great”), šarrūtīya “my kingship”. All of this is description; the wishes follow in the next lines.

sentences.i: A revolt that cannot be controlled (?), his hand, a curse (?), his ruin: in his dwelling may he scatter them for him,
sentences.n: Hard lines, which I read only as far as the words allow. tēši lā šubbîm: tēšû (Harper’s tešu “revolt”, te-ši) + lā + šubbîm, which Harper files under šabu II,1 “to attack, to control” (šu-ub-bi-im): “a revolt not to be controlled (?)”. qāssu raḫ: qāssu is qātum “hand” + -šu, the ss written with ZU (Harper’s ga-zu = qāssu); raḫ is listed by Harper as “curse” (his raḫlu): “his hand, a curse (?)”. ḫalāqišu “his perishing, his ruin” (the infinitive ḫalāqum + -šu); ina šubtišu “in his dwelling” (šubtum “dwelling” + -šu). lišappiḫaššum (Harper’s li-ša-ab-bi-ḫa-aš-šum) is li- + the D of sapāḫum “to scatter, to drive out” + -am (the ventive) + -šum “for him”, the m assimilated (-aš-šum): “let him scatter them for him”. How the pieces fit is UNCERTAIN; the five lines divide as Harper’s ruled lines do (59 te-ši la šu-ub-bi-im, with the last two signs in a sub-row; 60 ga-zu ra-aḫ; 61; 62; 63 with ḫa-aš-šum in a sub-row).

sentences.i: A reign of sighing, few days, years of famine, darkness without light, death of a glance of the eye (?) —
sentences.n: A list of the god’s gifts to the cursed man, all objects of lišīmšum (most of the endings show no case) in the next unit (“may he decree them for him as his fate”). palê tanēḫim: palûm “reign” (the BAL sign, Harper’s palû) and tanēḫum “sighing” (Harper’s taneḫu; the genitive after palê). ūmī iṣūtim: ūmī is the sign UD “days” (ûmi in Harper’s print marks a Sumerogram), iṣūtim the feminine plural of Harper’s isu “small, few”, written i-zu-tim with ZU for ṣu: “few days”. šanāt ḫušaḫḫim: šanāt is the plural of šattum “year” before a genitive, ḫušaḫḫum “hunger, famine”. eklit lā nawārim: Harper’s eklitu “darkness” (written ik-li-it), then lā nawārim “of no light”. mūt nīṭil īnim: mūt is mūtum “death” (not mutum “husband”), nīṭil is Harper’s nitlu “look, staring”, īnim “of the eye”: literally “death of a look of the eye”; I keep it literal (a sudden death?), and the force is UNCERTAIN.

sentences.i: the ruin of his city, the scattering of his people, the carrying off (?) of his kingship, and that his name and mention of him not be brought into being in the land —
sentences.n: More decrees, now as nouns in the construct, objects of liqbi in the next unit. ḫalāq ālišu “the perishing of his city” (ḫalāqum, with URU-šu “his city”); našpuḫ nišīšu “the scattering of his people” (našpuḫum, the N infinitive; Harper lists na-aš-pu-uḫ as sapahu IV,1, under “to disperse, to drive out”, the same root as lišappiḫaššum at xlii 63); šarrūssu šūbilam “the carrying off (?) of his kingship”: šarrūssu is šarrūtum + -šu (the ss written ZU), and šūbilam, Harper’s šu-bi-lam, which his glossary does enter, under his abalu (wabālum) III,1 “to bring, to take away, to transport” (with šu-bu-lu at xviii 60–61, 67); I read it as the Š-stem of wabālum “to carry”, with an accusative -am, “the carrying off”: UNCERTAIN (the vowels of šu-bi-lam are not those of the infinitive šūbulum, so the form may be something else). šumšu u zikiršu “his name and his mention” (zikrum “name, mention”, Harper’s zikru “name, vow”), ina mātim lā šubšâm “in the land, not to cause to be”: šubšâm is the Š infinitive of bašûm (Harper’s basu III,1, su-ub-sa-a-am) with lā: “not to bring into being”, that is, that no name or mention of him be brought forth in the land. The force follows the Š-stem (“to cause to be”); Harper gives no sense for the form.

sentences.n: ina pīšu kabtim liqbi: pīšu is KA “mouth” + -šu “his” (Harper’s pî “mouth, command”), kabtim “heavy, mighty” (kabtum), and liqbi the precative of qabûm “to say” (Harper’s qibu I,1, li-iq-bi). sentences.i: may she have the overthrow of his land, the perishing of his people, the pouring out of his life like water set on him, at the command of Ellil the king.
sentences.n: The curse closes with three more nouns in the construct, the objects of the verb at the end. šulpūt mātišu “the overthrow of his land” (šulputum, Harper’s lapatu III,1 “to smite, overturn”); ḫalāq nišīšu “the perishing of his people”; tabāk napištišu “the pouring out of his life” (tabākum “to pour out”, napištum “life”; the sign Harper reads piš is his sign list no. 134, kir/piš, the GÍR sign, so the word is spelt na-GÍR-ti-šu); kīma mê “like water”. ina pî Ellil šarrim “at the mouth, by the command, of Ellil the king”: KA is pî, {d}EN.LÍL is Ellil, and šarrim is “of the king” in apposition (a name is not inflected, so the genitive shows on the title). lišaškin is li- + the Š of šakānum “to set”, “let her cause to be set”, the subject being the goddess of xlii 81, and “on him” being understood. The sentence ends here; the next god (Ea, written {d}EN.KI) is called on at xlii 98.

glossary.-ša: her / its (3rd-person feminine suffix) · on nouns, “her”: after a t the š is assimilated and said ss, spelled with the sign ZA: bīssa (bi-za, or É-za) “her house”, mussa (mu-za) “her husband”, warkassa (wa-ar-ka-za) “her case”, bēlissa (be-li-za) “her mistress”; otherwise written plainly: panīša, mutiša, abiša, šeriqtaša, bēltiša · on an infinitive, the object “her”: ṣabātiša “seizing her” · on a verb-like form: ezibša (e-zi-ib-ša, UNCERTAIN in form) · on a plural noun: mārūša (DUMU{meš}-ša) “her sons”
glossary.-šina: their (3rd-person feminine plural possessive, on a noun): rēʾūssina “their shepherding”; after a t the š is assimilated (rēʾūt + -šina said rēʾūssina)
glossary.-šu: his / him · -šum “to him, for him” (dative): išakkanūšum, innadnušum · after a dental the suffix is assimilated and spelled with z: …ssu (ṣibat-zu, ṣibassu “its interest”, written after a broken sign); with a noun: ṣibtišu “its interest”, qātīšu “his hand”, damqaršu “his merchant”; tu-šu, te-šu in broken forms · with the same assimilation after a t: aššassu (aš-ša-zu) “his wife”, from aššat + -šu, t + š said ss · on a verb, the object “him”, or “to him” in the dative (Harper writes -šu for -šum): imaggarūšu (i-ma-ag-ga-ru-šu) “they shall agree to him”; on a noun after a preposition: elišu “upon him” · on a Š-stem, “him”: ušaḫḫazūšu “they shall have him take”, ušeṣṣûšu “they shall make him go out” · uktarriṣṣu (ug-dar-ri-zu) “he has slandered him” (ṣ + š said ṣṣ, spelled with ZU) · ikassûšuma “they shall bind him, and” · on nouns: emišu “his father-in-law’s”, ibiršu “his friend”, rabītišu “his senior one”, warkassu “his case”, zittišu “his share”, īnšu “his eye” · after a t, on a verb: uštāḫissu (uš-ta-ḫi-zu) “he has taught him” (the z of the stem + -šu said ss, spelled ZU); on nouns bīssu (É-ba/zu) “his house” and the participles murabbīšu, murabbītišu, murabbīssu “the one who raised him”; on a verb, ilqûšu, urtabbišu, urabbûšu, imtanûšu “him”; on the noun lišānšu (EME-šu) “his tongue”, īnšu “his eye”, mêšu “his waters”, mārūtišu “his sonship” · on a noun: bēlšu (be-el-šu), bēlišu (be-li-šu) “his master”, warḫušu (ITI-šu) “his month”, uznašu (u-zu-un-šu) “his ear”, nādinānšu (na-di-na-an-šu) “his seller”, nādinānišu (na-di-na-ni-šu) “his seller” after ana · written ZU in ARAD-zu, GEME₂-zu (warassu, amassu “his male slave, his female slave”) · on a verb, “him”: ukānšuma (u-ka-an-šu-ma) “he shall convict him, and” · also “its” on a Sumerogram or plural noun: GIŠ.PA-šu ḫaṭṭašu “his scepter”, SUḪUŠ-šu išdāšu “its foundations”, libbašu, libbišu “his heart”, bēlišu “his lord”, rēšīšu “its head”, dīnšu “his case”
glossary.-šum: to him, for him (dative suffix -šum, on a verb): ibaššišum “there is to him”, iqbišum “he said to him”, inaddiššum “he shall give him” · after d the suffix is assimilated and spelled ZUM: ipqissum (ip-qi₂-zum) “he entrusted to him” · ušēdišumma (u-še-di-šum-ma) “he made known to him, and”
glossary.Bēlit: Bēlit, “the lady”, the goddess, consort of Bêl (Harper’s Bêlit [NIN.LIL], written with the star, NIN and KID): the name is Harper’s reading of the sign group, not a spelling met in the text
glossary.Ekur: Ekur, “Mountain House” — Enlil’s temple at Nippur
glossary.Enlil: Enlil ({d}EN.LÍL) — lord of the lands, chief of the pantheon’s executive · said Ellil, written {d}EN.LÍL (the star + EN + KID), which Harper prints as Bêl “lord” (his glossary BEL [EN.LIL]); also Ellil šarrim “Ellil the king”
glossary.ZI.IM.RI.GA: UNREAD: four signs Harper prints in capitals without a reading; no meaning is claimed
glossary.abum: father: ilik abišu “his father’s fief-duty” · abī (a-bi) construct “father of”: abī mārtim “the father of the daughter” · abim written a-ba in bīt abim (Harper’s spelling, UNCERTAIN) · abu (a-bu) the form before a genitive “father of”: abu ilī “father of the gods”
glossary.adārum: to fear, be afraid (Harper’s adaru): idūrma (i-dur-ma, preterite + -ma) “he has feared, and”; lā idūrma “and has not feared”
glossary.ana: to, for · with an infinitive, “to, for” (ana kirîm zaqāpim “to plant as an orchard”); “as” (ana kirîm), “into” (ana libbi), “at the rate of” (ana itêšu) · also “over” (ana ālīya “over my city”), “before” in ana maḫar “into the presence of”; of time, ana dār “for ever”, ana warki “hereafter”, ana matīma “whenever”; ana lā + infinitive “so as not to”
glossary.arākum-D: D-stem of arākum “to be long” (Harper’s ARIKU II,1 “to prolong”): lirrik (li-ir-ri-ik, precative) “let him lengthen”, said of the scepter
glossary.arārum: to curse (Harper’s araru I,1): lirur (li-ru-ur, precative) “let him curse”
glossary.awātum: word, statement, matter · awâtim (a-wa-a-tim, plural genitive) “of words”: ana awâtim “to the words” · awâtīya (a-wa-ti-ia) and awâtūa (a-wa-tu-u-a) “my words” (plural + -ia) · awāssu (a-wa-zu, with -šu “his”, the ss written ZU) “his word”
glossary.awīlum: man; the free citizen, the code’s first legal class
glossary.awīlūtum: mankind, a person, the human race (Harper’s awilutu): awīlūtum (a-wi-lu-tum) in lū … ù lū awīlūtum “or any person”
glossary.ašrum: place; ana ašrišu “to its (proper) place” · ašar “where”, with a verb in the subjunctive: ašar illiku “where he went”
glossary.aššum: because (of); concerning · because; with a clause, also “so that”, giving purpose or reason (aššum … lā ṣabātiša, UNCERTAIN in grammar)
glossary.aḫāzum-Š: Š-stem of aḫāzum “to take”: to make take, have (a man) take (a wife): ušaḫḫazūšu (u-ša-aḫ-ḫa-zu-šu) “they shall have him take (a wife)” (present plural + -šu “him”) · uštāḫissu (uš-ta-ḫi-zu) “he has taught him”, Š-stem perfect with -šu “him”, the z of the stem and š said ss, spelled with ZU: šipir qātīšu uštāḫissu “he has taught him the work of his hands”; the Š-stem here is “to make learn”
glossary.bašûm-Š: Š-stem of bašûm “to exist”: to bring into being, produce (a crop): uštabši “he has produced” (perfect) · uštabši (uš-tab-ši) “he has brought about” (perfect): kazzatam uštabši “he has brought about a harm (?)” · ušabšû (u-ša-ab-šu-u) “which he brought about” (preterite + relative -u) · šubšâm (šu-ub-ša-a-am, Š infinitive, accusative) “to bring into being”: lā šubšâm “not to bring into being”, Harper’s basu III,1 (su-ub-sa-a-am), with no sense given by him
glossary.bêlum-Š: UNCERTAIN: Š-stem of Harper’s bêlu III “to overrule” (not the noun bēlum “lord”): uštepiel (uš-te-pi-el) “he has overruled (set aside)”, said of the king’s words; the root, the vowels and the tense of the spelling are not settled, and the sense is Harper’s
glossary.bēltum: lady, mistress (the feminine of bēlum): bēltiša (be-el-ti-ša) “her mistress”; bēlissa (be-li-za) “her mistress”, from the construct bēlit + -ša, t + š said ss · bēltum written with the single sign NIN, “lady”
glossary.bēlum: owner, lord: bēl ḫulqim “owner of the lost property” · owner of a field, bēl eqlim; bēl ḫubullim “creditor” · bēl kirîm “owner of the orchard” · bēl (be-el), the construct “owner of”, also with a suffix on the noun that follows: bēl ḫubullišu “his creditor”, bēl ḫubulliša “her creditor” · bēl (be-el, not the sign EN) “owner of”: bēl aššatim “the owner of the wife”, i.e. the man entitled to her (my reading) · bēlišu (be-li-šu) “its owner” (of an animal), bēlišuma “to its owner only” (with the emphatic -ma); bēl alpim “the owner of the ox” · bēl epinnim “the owner of the plough”, bēl tarbaṣim “the owner of the pen”; bēlīšunu (be-li-šu-nu) “their owners”, the owners of the cattle and sheep a herdsman has lost · bēl (be-el) “owner of” before a genitive: bēl wardim “the owner of the male slave” · bēlī (be-li) “my master”: ul bēlī atta “you are not my master” · bēlšu, bēlišu (be-el-šu, be-li-šu) “his master”
glossary.damāqum-D: D-stem of damāqum “to be good”: to show favor, be gracious (Harper’s damaku II “to favor”): lidammiqū (li-dam-mi-qu₂, precative, 3rd plural, KU read qu₂) “may they show favor” · mudammiqat (mu-dam-mi-qa₂-at, D participle, feminine) “she who makes good, who favors”: bēltum mudammiqat igirrīya “the lady who makes my igirrû favorable”
glossary.diānum: to judge: dīnam idīn “he judged a case” · adīnu (a-di-nu) “I judged” (first person preterite + relative -u, filed by Harper under dânum “to judge”; the same word was read addinu, nadānum, in the part before): dīn adīnu “the verdict I judged” · lidīn (li-di-in, precative) “let him judge”
glossary.dīnum: case, lawsuit; judgment: dīn napištim “a case of life” · dīnāt (di-na-a-at, plural, the form before a genitive) “judgments of”; dīn mātim “the case of the land”
glossary.egirrûm: UNCERTAIN: Harper’s egirru “dreams, plans”, the sense in this line unclear: igirrê (i-gi-ir-ri-e, plural, oblique case) · igirrīya (with -ia “my”) “my igirrû” (plans? dreams?), UNCERTAIN
glossary.ekletum: darkness (Harper’s eklitu): eklit (ik-li-it) in eklit lā nawārim “darkness without light”
glossary.ela: UNCERTAIN: perhaps ēla “except, apart from” (e-la), a guess from the spelling; Harper prints a footnote with another reading and the stretch is unread
glossary.emqum: wise, skilled · imkim (im-ki-im, Harper’s IM-KI-IM (?)): perhaps emqim “of the wise one” (the litany’s im-qum is said emqum), UNCERTAIN, the reading is the drafter’s suggestion and not Harper’s
glossary.ešērum: to be straight; Št-stem šutēšurum “to guide aright”; mušūšer · uštēšir (uš-te-še-ir, perfect) “he has set right”; šūtešurim (infinitive) “to set right” · lištēšir (li-iš-te-še-ir, Št precative) “let him guide aright”: ṣalmāt qaqqadišu lištēšir “let him guide his black-headed people aright” · šutēšuram (šu-te-šu-ra-am, Št infinitive, accusative) “to guide aright”: mātassu šutēšuram ileʾʾi “he is able to guide his land aright”
glossary.ilum: god; here: the temple as owner · plural ilāni “gods” (written DINGIR.DINGIR, as in the litany): maḫar ilāni “before the gods” · ilum (the AN sign alone, DINGIR) “the god”, the god not named in the line · ilī (written NI.NI, two triangle signs, Harper’s List no. 99) “gods”: irrīt ilī “the curse of the gods”, abu ilī “father of the gods”
glossary.ina: in, from · at (ina ebūrim “at harvest”); out of (ina bilat kirîm “out of the orchard’s yield”) · “through, by (means of)”: ina maḫāṣim “through beating”, ina pilšim “by a breach”; “regarding”: ina mimma ša … “regarding whatever …”; ina šanat “in the year” · “with, by”, of company or means (UNCERTAIN): ina liātim “with (or by) the cattle” · also “with, by means of” (ina kakkim dannim “with the mighty weapon”, ina igigallim “with wisdom”), “by” with kibīt “command” and awāt “word” (the authority), “in” a manner (ina damiqtim “in favor”, ina šulmim “in peace”)
glossary.irritum: curse (Harper’s irritu): irrītīya (ir-ri-ti-ia) “my curses” (with -ia “my”) · irrīt (ir-ri-it, the form before a genitive) “the curse of” · irrītim (ir-ri-tim, genitive) “of the curse”: aššum irrītim šināti “because of those curses”
glossary.išûm: to have: lā īšu “he has not” · īšu “he has”, īšû (the subjunctive form, in a clause that continues): ana turrim lā īšû “has not to repay” · īša (i-na(=ša)) “he has”, UNCERTAIN: the carver wrote NA for ŠA and the form (īšu would be expected) is not accounted for
glossary.iṣûm: small, few (Harper’s isu “small”, written i-zu-tim with ZU for ṣu): iṣūtim (feminine plural) in ūmī iṣūtim “few days”; “few” is the sense that fits the line
glossary.kabtum: heavy; grave (of an offence): arnam kabtam (kab-tam, accusative) “a heavy offence” · of a wound, severe: ṣimmam kabtam (kab-tam, accusative) “a severe wound”
glossary.kabātum: to be heavy, be weighty, be potent (Harper’s kabatu I,1): kabtat (kab-ta-at, stative, 3rd feminine) “she is weighty”: ša kibīssa ina Ekur kabtat “whose command is weighty in Ekur”
glossary.kalāmum-D: D-stem of kalāmum (Harper: KALAMU, “to show, inform”): to show: ukallam (u-kal-lam, present) “he shall show”
glossary.kibsum: way, tread, procedure (Harper’s kibsu, from kabāsum “to tread”): kibsam (ki-ib-sa-am, accusative) “the way”
glossary.kibītum: speech, command (Harper’s kibitu): kibīt (ki-be-it, the form before a genitive) “command of” · kibīssu (ki-be-zu, with -šu “his”) “his command”; kibīssa (ki-be-za, with -ša “her”) “her command”; the ss is written with ZU and ZA
glossary.kittum: truth, right — kittum u mīšarum, “truth and justice” · kīnātim (ki-na-tim, plural) “truths”: Šamaš kīnātim išrukušum “Shamash gave him truths”
glossary.kīma: like, as · as, like; with a verb in the subjunctive: kīma ubbalu “as he brings (it)” · according to: kīma ṣimdat šarrim “according to the king’s schedule” · “since, when”, before a stative: kīma mimmûšu lā ḫalqu “since his goods are not lost” · “in proportion to”: kīma emūq zittiša “in proportion to the strength of her share”, kīma emūq bīt abim “in proportion to the means of her father’s house” · in place of, for (of animal for animal): alpam kīma alpim “an ox for an ox” (the §263 restitution)
glossary.lapātum-Š: Š-stem of lapātum “to smite, overturn” (Harper’s lapatu III,1): šulpūt (šu-ul-pu-ut, verbal noun before a genitive) “the overthrow of”: šulpūt mātišu “the overthrow of his land”
glossary.laḫa: UNREAD: la-ḫa, a word Harper gives as bare signs; no meaning is claimed
glossary.lemēnum-D: D-stem of lemēnum “to be evil” (Harper’s limenu II,1 “to be evil, hostile”): lilemmin (li-li-mi-in, precative) “let her make evil”
glossary.leʾûm: to be able: ileʾʾi “he is able” (Harper: i-li-i)
glossary.lā: not (in subordinate and nominal contexts) · before a noun in the genitive, “without”: lā kanīkim “without a sealed receipt”; in a šumma-clause, “not”: lā ītamar “he did not see” · before an infinitive, ana lā ḫabālim “so as not to wrong”
glossary.lū: or; either (lū … lū “whether … or”); with verb: “let …” · ù lu, two words written together, “or”: ù lu ina maḫāṣim “or through beating”
glossary.mašûm: to forget (Harper’s masu I,1): imēšma (i-me-eš-ma, Harper’s spelling; UNCERTAIN: a regular preterite of this verb would be expected as imši) “he has forgotten, and”
glossary.maḫar: before, in the presence of: maḫar ilim “before the god”
glossary.melammum: the awe-inspiring radiance of gods and kings
glossary.mû: water(s); mê nuḫšim “waters of abundance” · ina mêšu (ME-e-šu) “in his waters”, of a child taken while in the waters of birth, i.e. perhaps a newborn, the idiom UNCERTAIN; the form mê is the oblique of a plural-looking noun
glossary.mātum: land, country · māt (ma-at) the form before a following genitive, “the land of”: ina māt nukurtim “in a hostile country” · mātim (ma-tim, or the Sumerogram KALAM, no ending written) genitive “of the land”: ina libbu mātim “in the middle of the land”, mārū mātim “natives of the country”, mātim šanītim “another country” · mātassu (ma-zu, with -šu “his”, the t and š said ss and written with ZU) “his land”; mātišu (ma-ti-šu) “his land”
glossary.mūtum: death (mūtum; not mutum “husband”): mūt (mu-ut, the form before a genitive) “death of”
glossary.nakārum-D: D-stem of nakārum “to be strange, different”: to make different, change: uttakkir (ut-ta-ak-ki-ir, D perfect) “he has changed”: šimtam uttakkir “he has changed the mark (?)” (the object is UNCERTAIN; the verb is plain from the stem) · after ay: ay unakkir (u-na-ak-ki-ir, D preterite) “may he not change” · uttakkaru (ut-ta-ka-ru, with the subjunctive -u; Harper files it under nakaru II,2 beside the perfect uttakkir) “is altered”, the passive of the D, UNCERTAIN: ša kibīssu lā uttakkaru “whose command is not altered”
glossary.narûm: stele, inscribed monument (Harper’s naru “monument, inscription”): narûya (na-ru-ia; also na-ru-i, with -ia “my” written short) “my stele”
glossary.nasāḫum: to pull out, uproot; of a son, to cast out, disinherit (Harper: “to cut off, to disinherit”): nasāḫim (na-sa-ḫi-im, infinitive) “to cast out”; anassaḫ (a-na-za-aḫ) “I shall cast out” (first person present); inassaḫ (i-na-za-aḫ) “he shall cast out” (third person present) · inassaḫū (i-na-za-ḫu) “they shall pluck out”, present plural: īnšu inassaḫū “they shall pluck out his eye” (the ZA sign for sa) · nasāḫim (na-sa-ḫi-im) infinitive “to cast out”: ana tarbītim nasāḫim “to cast out the foster-child” · assuḫ (az-zu-uḫ, preterite, 1st person) “I tore out”, of enemies · lissuḫ (li-zu-uḫ, precative, the n assimilated and the ss written with ZU) “let him uproot”: raggam u ṣēnam lissuḫ “let him uproot the wicked and the evil one”
glossary.nawārum: to be bright; D-stem — munawwir “who brightens” · nawārim (na-wa-ri-im, genitive) “of light”: eklit lā nawārim “darkness without light”; Harper files it under namaru II,1 “to enlighten”, beside the prologue’s nuwwurim, UNCERTAIN in form
glossary.nazāqum-Š: Š-stem of nazāqum (Harper’s nazaku III “to cut off, efface, destroy”; the sense is not firm): to efface: mušazziqam (mu-ša-zi-qam, participle, accusative; KAM read qam) “one who effaces”, ušazziq (u-ša-zi-iq, preterite) “he effaced”; the stem and root are UNCERTAIN
glossary.našqum: weighty, choice (Harper’s našku): našqā (na-aš-qa₂, stative plural) “(they are) weighty” (GA read qa₂)
glossary.nišū: people; the household: nišīšu “his household” · nišīšu (ni-ši-šu) “his people”: nišīšu ina mīšarim lirʾi “let him shepherd his people in justice”; šīr nišīšu “the flesh of his people”
glossary.nīṭilum: UNCERTAIN: look, glance (Harper’s nitlu “look, staring”): nīṭil (ni-ṭi-il, the form before a genitive) in mūt nīṭil īnim “death of a glance of the eye (?)”; the force of the phrase is unsettled
glossary.palûm: reign, term of rule (the BAL sign, Harper’s List no. 7, palû): palêya (BALA-ia, with -ia “my”) “my reign” · palê (BALA, before a genitive) “the reign of”: palê tanēḫim “a reign of sighing”
glossary.parāsum: to decide, cut off: iprus · iparrasūma (i-par-ra-su-ma) “they shall investigate, and” (present plural + -ma; Harper: “to decide, to investigate, to inquire into”)
glossary.pasāsum-D: D-stem of pasāsum “to blot out, abolish” (Harper’s pasasu II,2): uptassis (up-ta-az-zi-is, D perfect, the double s written with z) “he has blotted out”
glossary.patesi: governor, ruler of a city (the Sumerian title PA.TE.SI, which Harper keeps as pa-te-si); written PA.TE.SI with three signs and said patesi
glossary.pašāṭum: to efface, rub out (Harper’s pasatu I,1): ipšiṭma (ip-ši-iṭ-ma, preterite + -ma) “he has erased, and”
glossary.purussûm: decision, verdict · purussâšina (pu-ru-za-ši-na, accusative singular + -šina “their”, the double s written with ZA) “their decision” · purussê (pu-ru-zi-e, oblique plural) “decisions of” · purussîm (pu-ru-zi-im, genitive) “of the decision”
glossary.pûm: mouth (the KA sign); ina pī mātim “in the mouth of the land” · ana pî ṣimdat šarrim “according to the mouth of the king’s ordinance” · ana pî riksātīšu “according to his contract”, literally “to the mouth of his binding terms” (KA read pî)
glossary.qabûm: to speak, say: iqbû, iqtabi, iqabbûma · iqabbi (written i-qa₂-ab-bi-ma, iqabbi + -ma; Harper prints the GA sign as ga, read qa₂) present “he shall say, declare”: ina maḫar ilim … iqabbima “he shall declare before the god” · liqbīma (li-iq-bi-ma, li- + iqbi + -ma) “let him say, and” · liqbi (li-iq-bi, precative) “let him say”: ina pīšu kabtim liqbi “with his weighty mouth let him say”
glossary.qaqqadum: head; the capital, the principal of a loan, as against its interest (written SAG.DU, “head”): ana qaqqadim “to the capital” (genitive, written with the logogram) · qaqqad kaspim “the capital of the silver” (construct form, here spelled ga-ga-ad)
glossary.qâlum: UNCERTAIN: to give heed, pay attention (Harper’s QALU “to give attention to”, written with the sign gul): liqūlma (li-gul-ma, precative, “let him pay heed, and”), iqūlma (i-gul-ma, preterite, “he has paid heed, and”; lā iqūlma “and has not heeded”); the root and the vowels are not settled, and the sense is Harper’s
glossary.qātum: hand: ina qāt “from the hand of” · qātīšu (qa₂-ti-šu) “of his hands”: bīš qātīšu “his own goods” · qāt (qa₂-at) construct “in the hand of, in the care of”: ina qāt mušēniqtim “in the care (hand) of the wet-nurse” · qātīšu “of his hands” in šipir qātīšu “the work of his hands” · ina qātišu (qa₂-ti-šu) “in his hand”: ittaṣbat ina qātišu “he was caught with it in his hand” · qāssu (qa₂-zu, with -šu “his”, the ss written with ZU) “his hand”
glossary.rabûm: great; D/Š-stems “make great”; rabûtim “great (pl.)” · rabîtim (ra-bi-tim, feminine genitive) “large”: ina abnim rabîtim “by the large stone” · rabītišu (ra-bi-ti-šu) “his senior one”, the feminine with -šu: read as the father’s chief wife, UNCERTAIN
glossary.rabûm-Š: Š-stem of rabûm “to be great” (Harper’s rabu III,1 “to enlarge, make great”): mušarbû (mu-šar-bu-u, Š participle) “one who makes great”: mušarbû šarrūtīya “who makes my kingship great”
glossary.raḫlum: UNCERTAIN: curse (Harper’s raḫlu): raḫ (ra-aḫ) in qāssu raḫ “his hand, a curse (?)”; the form is cut short and its place in the sentence is unclear
glossary.rêʾûm-pasture: to pasture, graze (a herd): the infinitive in the genitive after ana, ana … rēʾîm “to pasture” (ri-im), said rēʾîm; the spelling ri-im is Harper’s and the reading of the word as the infinitive of rêʾûm (the verb behind rēʾûm “shepherd”) is my own from the grammar, UNCERTAIN · lirʾi (li-ri, precative) “let him shepherd”: nišīšu ina mīšarim lirʾi “let him shepherd his people in justice”; the spelling li-ri has no sign for the ʾ, and Harper files it under another verb (ARU II,1 “to carry, to rule”), so the reading is UNCERTAIN
glossary.rīdum: leading, guidance, government (Harper’s ridu “government”, a noun of redûm “to lead”): rīdam (ri-dam, accusative) “guidance”
glossary.sapāḫum-D: D-stem of sapāḫum “to scatter”: to scatter, neglect (Harper: “to scatter, to neglect”), said of a house or household: uzappaḫ (u-za-ap-pa-aḫ, present, 3rd person) · lišappiḫaššum (li-ša-ab-bi-ḫa-aš-šum, precative + the ventive -am + -šum “for him”, m + š said šš; Harper’s sapahu II,1) “let him scatter (them) for him”
glossary.sapāḫum-N: N-stem of sapāḫum “to scatter” (Harper lists na-aš-pu-uḫ as sapahu IV,1, under “to disperse, to drive out”): našpuḫ (na-aš-pu-uḫ) “the scattering”, a verbal noun before a genitive, našpuḫ nišīšu “the scattering of his people”
glossary.tabākum: to pour out (Harper enters ta-ba-ak as the noun tabku “pouring out”): tabāk (ta-ba-ak, infinitive before a genitive) “the pouring out of”: tabāk napištišu “the pouring out of his life”
glossary.tanādātum: UNCERTAIN: tanādātim (ta-na-da-tim, genitive) “might, tyranny” (Harper’s tanatu, the d spelled for t); the reading and the sense are unsettled
glossary.tanēḫum: sighing, groaning (Harper’s taneḫu): tanēḫim (ta-ne-ḫi-im, genitive) in palê tanēḫim “a reign of sighing”
glossary.târum-D: D-stem of târum: to give back: turru “taken away/captured”; utarrūšumma “they shall return (it) to him” · utâr (present) “he shall hand back” · turrim (infinitive, tu-ur-ri-im): ana turrim “for repaying, to give back”; utâr (present) “he shall hand back” · uttēr (ut-te-ir, perfect) “he has given back”: the same verb as utâr · litēršu (li-te-ir-šu, precative + -šu, Harper’s taru II,1) “let him turn back / take back from him”, UNCERTAIN: melam šarrūtim litēršu “let him turn the glory of kingship away from him”
glossary.tēšûm: UNCERTAIN: revolt (Harper’s tešu “revolt”): tēšī (te-ši, said with a long ī; the case ending in the construct is not known) in a phrase that is itself uncertain
glossary.ummum: mother: ana ummišu “to his mother”, ummašu urabbāšu “his mother shall raise him” · ummātim (um-ma-tim) plural “mothers”: ana ummātim “by mothers”; ummātišunu “their mothers”
glossary.wabālum-Š: Š-stem of wabālum “to carry”: to make carry off, let (water) carry away: uštābil (perfect) “he has let (the water) carry off” · ušābilšu (u-ša-bil-šu, preterite) “he had (him) carry”; šūbulu (šu-bu-lu, Š stative šūbul with the subjunctive -u) “(what) has been sent”, šūbulūma (šu-bu-lu-ma) “has been sent, and”; the stative reading is from the form and the exact sense is UNCERTAIN · ušābil (u-ša-bi-il) “he has had (a present) brought” (preterite, without -u where there is no ša); ušābilu (u-ša-bi-lu) “who had (a present) brought” (with the relative -u) · šūbilam (šu-bi-lam) “the carrying off (?)”: šarrūssu šūbilam “the carrying off (?) of his kingship”; Harper enters it under abalu III,1 “to bring, to take away, to transport”, but the vowels are not those of the infinitive, so the form is UNCERTAIN
glossary.waṣûm-Š: Š-stem of waṣûm “to go out”: to send out, bring out; of land, to take on lease: ana irrišūtim ušēṣi “he took (a field) for cultivation” · ušeṣṣûšu (u-še-iz-zu-u-šu) “they shall make him go out” (present plural + -šu “him”; Harper writes ṣ as z): ālam ušeṣṣûšu “they shall drive him out of the city” · šuṣâ (šu-ṣa-a; Harper’s su-sa-a, under III,1) “brought out (?)”: the form (a stative plural? an imperative?) and its subject are UNCERTAIN
glossary.ālum: city (URU): ālum u rabiānum “the city and the mayor”
glossary.īnum: eye: īnšu … iššīma “he lifted his eye (to it)” — he coveted it · ša īnšu maḫru (i-in-šu) “whose eye is first” = the son he favours (UNCERTAIN idiom)
glossary.Šamaš: Shamash ({d}UTU) — the sun-god, lord of justice
glossary.ša: who, which, of · also “whose”: ša + a noun with its own suffix + the verb at the end (ša ḫaṭṭašu išarat “whose scepter is straight”), the verb in the subjunctive
glossary.šabûm-D: UNCERTAIN: D-stem of Harper’s šabu (II,1 “to attack, to control”): šubbîm (šu-ub-bi-im) in tēšī lā šubbîm “a revolt not to be controlled (?)”; the form and the sense are unsettled
glossary.šakānum-Š: Š-stem of šakānum “to set, place”: lišaškin (li-ša-aš-ki-in, precative) “let her cause to be set”, said of a curse laid on a man
glossary.šanûm: another, a second one: ana šanîm “to another”, šanûm “another man” · feminine šanītum “another (woman)”: šanītam, šanītim (ša-ni-tam, ša-ni-tim), in the accusative and genitive · šaniam (ša-ni-a-am, accusative) “another”: šaniam ul uppal “nor shall she pay another (?)”, UNCERTAIN · šanītim (ša-ni-tim) feminine genitive “another”, agreeing with mātim: mātim šanītim “another country”
glossary.šanānum: to rival (Harper’s šananu): šāninam (ša-ni-nam, accusative) “a rival”; the clause it stands in is UNCERTAIN
glossary.šarrum: king: šarrum “the king”, šar-ri-im “of the king”
glossary.šarākum: to give away, hand over: ištarak · išruk (iš-ru-uq) “he has given (as a gift)” (the last sign UG, read uq or uk)
glossary.šattum: year: šattam (syllabic, §31) or MU (the year-sign, §30) · šattim (genitive); plural šanātim “years” (ša šanātim “of the years”); MU 4{kam}, said erbe šanātim “four years” · MU 3{kam}, said šalāš šanātim “for three years”; šanat (ša-na-at) “(in) the year”, ina šanat “each year”
glossary.šaṭrum: written, inscribed (the passive participle of šaṭārum “to write”): šaṭram (ša-aṭ-ra-am, accusative) “inscribed”, said of narûm “stele”
glossary.šaṭārum: to write; to assign in writing, deed over (Harper: išaddar): ul išaddar “he shall not deed” · išṭuršum (iš-tur-šum) “he wrote for him”: kunukkam išṭuršum “he wrote him a sealed document” · išṭurušim (iš-tu-ru-ši-im, with the subjunctive -u in a ša-clause), išṭuršim (iš-tur-ši-im), išṭuršimma (iš-tur-ši-im-ma) “he wrote for her (and)”, preterite + -šim: ina ṭuppim ša išṭurušim “in the tablet which he wrote for her”, lā išṭuršimma “he has not written for her, and” · ištadar (iš-ta-dar, perfect; Harper files it under šataru I,2, and DAR is written dar as he has it, as in išaddar) “he has written”: šumšu ištadar “his name he has written”
glossary.šebērum: to break: ištebir (iš-te-bi-ir, perfect, 3rd singular) “he has broken”, išebbirū (i-še-ib-bi-ru, present, 3rd plural, with the b doubled) “they shall break” · verb · išbir (iš-bi-ir, preterite, 3rd singular) “he has broken” · lišbir (li-iš-bi-ir, precative) “let him break”: ḫaṭṭašu lišbir “let him break his scepter”
glossary.šipṭum: judgment (Harper’s šiptu): šipṭim (ši-ip-di-im, genitive, DI written for ṭi) in ašar šipṭim ù purussîm “the place of judgment and decision”
glossary.šumma: if — the word that opens every law of the code
glossary.šâmum: to buy: ištām “he bought”, išammu “he buys” · ALSO a second verb of the same spelling, “to fix, decree” (destinies, well-being): išīm (i-ši-im) “he decreed”, išīmam (i-ši-ma-am) “he decreed for me” (preterite + the ventive -am)
glossary.šâmum-D: D-stem of šâmum “to fix, decide” (Harper’s samu II,1): mušīm (mu-ši-im, D participle before a genitive) “one who fixes”: mušīm šīmātim “who fixes the fates”
glossary.šīmtum: fate; one’s natural death: ana šīmtim ittalak “he went to (his) fate” = he died · plural šīmātum “fates”: šīmātīša (ši-ma-ti-ša) “her fates”; ina šīmātīša imtūt “she died in her fates” = she died a natural death
glossary.šīrum: flesh, body; wellbeing · šīr (SU, bound form before a genitive) “flesh of”: šīr pasuttišu “the flesh of its pasuttu”
glossary.šū: he, that (šū/šuāti “that (man)”) · šināti (ši-na-ti, feminine plural, oblique) “those”: aššum irrītim šināti “because of those curses”
glossary.ūmum: day; ūmišu “daily” (written UD-mi-šu) · plural “days”: ūmī (written UD-mi-) “days”: ina ūmīšu lā malûtim “in his days not full” (the days of a lease) · ūm “day” (UD), before a following word, in ūm NER lā “a day (when ?) NER not …” · ūmīšu (UD-mi-šu) “his days”: ūmīšu imannûma “they shall count his days” · ina ūmim (i-na UD) “per day, by the day”, with the numeral 1{kam}: ina ūmim 1{kam} 180 qa “for each day 180 qa”; the day-rate formula of §271–277 · ūmī (the sign UD alone) “days”: ūmī iṣūtim “few days”
glossary.Ḫammurabi: Hammurabi, king of Babylon c. 1792–1750 BCE (Amorite name, “the kinsman is great”)
glossary.ḫalāqum: to be lost, vanish: ḫalqu, ḫalqam · iḫtaliq (iḫ-ta-li-iq, perfect) “it has been lost”; ḫaliq (ḫa-li-iq, stative) “(it) is lost”, ḫaliqma “is lost, and”; lā ḫaliqma “is not lost, and”
glossary.ḫaṭṭum: scepter · written GIŠ.PA-šu, said ḫaṭṭašu “his scepter”
glossary.ḫušaḫḫum: hunger, famine (Harper’s ḫušaḫḫu): ḫušaḫḫim (ḫu-ša-aḫ-ḫi-im, genitive) in šanāt ḫušaḫḫim “years of famine”
glossary.ṣalmum-black: black, dark: ṣalmāt (ṣa-al-ma-at, plural before a genitive) in ṣalmāt qaqqadišu “his black-headed people” (Harper: “Black-Head race, i.e. mankind”), the phrase of the prologue (ṣalmāt qaqqadim) spelt out in syllables
glossary.ṣēnum: sheep, the flock: ṣēnē over the sheep-sign LU · also written U₈.UDU{ḫi.a} (ewe + sheep + plural marker): ṣēnū, ṣēnī · ṣēnam (ṣi-nam, accusative) “evil (one)”, a different noun from ṣēnum “sheep” (the prologue’s ṣēnum “evil (one)”): raggam u ṣēnam “the wicked and the evil one”
glossary.ṭâbum-D: to make good, to content, satisfy (literally “make the heart good”): libbaša uṭabbū (u-ṭa-ab-bu) “they shall content her”, D-stem present plural; uṭṭibbū (uṭ-ṭi-ib-bu) “they have contented (her)”, D-stem perfect, the form UNCERTAIN because of the doubled b · verb, D-stem · liṭīb (li-ṭi-ib, precative) “let him make good”: šīr nišīšu liṭīb “let him bring well-being to his people”, literally “let him make good the flesh of his people”
